segments.text: Gumgumi pulls an old, yellowed book off the shelf and opens it.
Even set right beside a new book, nothing has touched it.
Paper still holds a substance that once glued wood fibers together.
Meeting air and light, it slowly turns into something else.
That new substance reflects a lot more yellow light.
Newsprint holds way more of that substance.
So it turns yellow much faster, within days.
That's why old paper turns yellow over time.
